analysis.evidence: קֵינָן is the subject of וַיְחִי. אַחֲרֵי הוֹלִידוֹ אֶת מַהֲלַלְאֵל marks the starting point, and the following year count gives the duration. Kenan lived 840 years after he fathered Mahalalel.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third-person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־ and no suffix.
analysis.sense: continue living for a stated period

draft.definition: Kenan, the son of Enosh in Genesis 5:9.
draft.evidence: וַיּוֹלֶד אֶת קֵינָן identifies Kenan as the child Enosh fathered.

analysis.evidence: In וַיְחִי קֵינָן, Kenan is the subject of “lived.” The phrase אַחֲרֵי הוֹלִידוֹ אֶת מַהֲלַלְאֵל identifies him as Mahalalel’s father, continuing the genealogy of Enosh’s son.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular proper noun, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: The personal name of the son of Enosh.

analysis.evidence: אַחֲרֵי governs הוֹלִידוֹ אֶת מַהֲלַלְאֵל, “his fathering Mahalalel.” It marks the event after which Kenan lived another 840 years.
analysis.morphology: Preposition in the plural construct form אַחֲרֵי, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: אַחֲרֵי introduces the time clause “after he fathered Mahalalel.” The suffix ־וֹ refers to Kenan, and אֶת marks Mahalalel as the direct object.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil infinitive construct with a third-person masculine singular suffix marking the subject, Kenan.

analysis.evidence: In אַחֲרֵי הוֹלִידוֹ אֶת מַהֲלַלְאֵל, “after he fathered Mahalalel,” אֶת marks the personal name מַהֲלַלְאֵל as the definite direct object of הוֹלִידוֹ.
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: Kenan is the subject of וַיְחִי. The phrase אַחֲרֵי הוֹלִידוֹ אֶת מַהֲלַלְאֵל means “after he fathered Mahalalel,” identifying Mahalalel as Kenan’s son.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular proper noun without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: אַרְבָּעִים modifies שָׁנָה ‘year’. The following וּשְׁמֹנֶה מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה adds eight hundred years, giving the 840 years Kenan lived after fathering Mahalalel.
analysis.morphology: Cardinal numeral, plural absolute, common to both genders, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In אַרְבָּעִים שָׁנָה, the marked noun supplies the unit for “forty.” These forty years form part of the 840 years Kenan lived after fathering Mahalalel.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular absolute noun, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: שְׁמֹנֶה counts the hundreds in מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה. The conjunction joins these eight hundred years to the preceding אַרְבָּעִים שָׁנָה, giving 840 years.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וּ־ prefixed to the feminine singular absolute cardinal numeral שְׁמֹנֶה.
analysis.sense: eight as the multiplier of hundreds

analysis.evidence: In וּשְׁמֹנֶה מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה, שְׁמֹנֶה counts eight hundreds and שָׁנָה supplies the unit. Together with the preceding אַרְבָּעִים שָׁנָה, the verse gives 840 years.
analysis.morphology: Cardinal numeral, plural absolute, with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: hundreds (plural מֵאוֹת, with the digits: three hundred to nine hundred)

analysis.evidence: In וּשְׁמֹנֶה מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה, the marked noun supplies the unit for “eight hundred.” Together with the preceding forty years, it gives the 840 years Kenan lived after fathering Mahalalel.
Kenan (קֵינָן) is the subject, and בָּנִים וּבָנוֹת (“sons and daughters”) are the direct objects of וַיּוֹלֶד. After fathering Mahalalel, Kenan fathered other children.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil wayyiqtol, third-person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ and no suffix
